(i) the electrolyte pH is a key factor for bubble-free delamination of graphene; (ii) graphene delamination is possible at pH 4, which is lower than the pH at which hydrogen bubbles are formed, and (iii) the bubble-free delamination method enables the production of large amounts (up to 1000 cm2) of high quality graphene with low sheet resistance and high carrier mobility.

The production of large amounts (several mL) of hydrogen bubbles, which is typical of electrochemical methods for graphene delamination based on water electrolysis, results in mechanical and chemical damage to graphene films, and the production of defect-rich graphene.
